PLASTICS -- METHODS OF TESTING
PART 8 PERMANENCEICHEMICAL PROPERTIES Section 14 Determination of the Effects of Exposure to Damp Heat, Water Spray and Salt Mist

O 0.1

Introduction

Various test methods are available for the exposure of plastics to different aggressive agents acting in a combined and simultaneous fashion, such as natural weathering. Other test methods are available for the purpose of a separate evaluation of the action of individual aggressive agents. Among the latter there are, for example, tests for the resistance to specific chamicals and to radiations of a definite spectral range. For some applications, it may be desirable to evaluate the behaviour of the materials in a hot damp atmosphere just below the saturation limit of water vapour, as well as in the presence of the liquid phase. In these conditions not only water absorption or leaching of some ingredients of the compositiorl may be observed but also degradation phenomena due to hydrolysis, exudation of plasticizers, etc. It may aLsobe desirable sometimes to evaluate the behaviour of materials in the presence of a highly corrosive electrolyte, such as a sodium chloride solution (salt mist), which is the principal aggressive agent present in marine environments and of particular importance in the case of nautical applications. It is well known that sodium chloride has no noticeable action on the polymers that are the basic components of plastics, and that salt solutions, owing to their higher osmotic pressure, are normally absorbed by plaatica to a lesser degree than pure water, but it cannot be assumed a priori that they have no action on composite materials, containing fillers, reinforcing components or pigments, for instance.

and have been described by International Standards relevant to other materials and IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission) standards relevant to electrical and electronic components. The same equipment and procAuras described in these standarda can also be employed for plastics, with appropriate care and adjustments.

0.3

The present International Standard is intended to provide general guidance only, on the choice of suitable equipment and procedures for obtaining the exposure conditions described above and for the preparation of test specimens. It also only gives general guidance on the properties to be evaluated. Specific details are given in the various ISO and IEC Publications.

For the expression of results, the present International Stendard follows, as far as possible, the same criteria adopted in the existing test methods for the exposure to chemicala (see ISO 175) and to natural weathering or artificial light (see 1s0 e). 0.4 These tests are intended to yield data about the effects of the described exposures ,on the materials; however, a direct correlation between the experimental results and the behaviour . in service is not to be inferred.

Annex Absorption of moisture by a test specimen in equilibrium with its conditioning of a plastics atmosphere material

(This annex forma an integral part of the standard.)

A. 1

The amount and rate of absorption of moisture by a test specimen conditioned in a humid atmosphere varies significantly according to the nature of the plastics material tasted.

A.3 In these two cases one of two followed : A.3.1

procedures

can be

A.2

The normal conditions for conditioning established in this International Standard (see 4.4) are generally satisfactory, except for the following:

Drying the material at elevated temperature. This procedure has the dmdvantage that certain properties, mechanical in particular, in the dry state dtier from those obtained after conditioning at 23 * 2 "C and (50 + 5) % r.h.

A.3.2 A.2. 1
Materials known to reach equilibrium with their conditioning atmosphere only after a very long period of time (for example, certain polyamides).

Conditioning the teat specimen at 23 + 2 `C and (50 * 5) % r.h. until equilibrium is achieved. In this case, a suitable criterion could be one of the following: a) Maaa constant wkhin 0,1 % for two determinations aepereted by an interval of d2 weeks (d titng the thickness of the teat specimen in millkrwtrea). b) For certain polymers, it is sufficient to plot the graph of mass against time, with intervals much leaa than d2 weeks, equilibrium being considered achieved for practical purpoaea whpn the gradient of the curve, expressed as a percentage, is equal to 0,1 %.

A.2.2

New materials or those of unknown structure, for

which no a pn"ori forecast can be made either of their capacity for absorbing moisture or of the time required for reaching equilibrium.

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
